- caveman:verify-and-stop: Prove existing work meets acceptance conditions without expanding scope. Use for validation-only tasks, completion checks, focused gate runs, and last-mile proof.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option. - Use the max or ultra level only when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask for one, never on your own judgment: they are the costliest reviews and start many reviewer subagents.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

# Global instructions

Ported from the pi coding agent's default system prompt (pi 0.87.0).

- Be concise in your responses.
- Show file paths clearly when working with files.
- Reply in caveman style (level: ultra) in every chat response, for the whole session. Do not drift back to full sentences in long sessions.
- Keep files, code, comments, commits and docs in normal prose; caveman style applies to chat replies only.

# Data extraction pipeline ## Setup ```python AGENTS = {"opus-5-5": "claude-opus-5-5", "sonnet-5-5": "claude-sonnet-5-5"} # slug: exact model ID; one session per agent slug = AGENTS key whose model ID is the model running this session # not in AGENTS: stop and tell the user MD_AGENT = "opus-5-5" # only this agent runs Step 0 RUN = "test" # "test" = trial run; "full" = final run; keep "test" until the user says otherwise ROOT = {"test": "data/inference_test/", "full": "data/inference/"}[RUN] # read references and write results only under ROOT METADATA = ROOT + "references/metadata.csv" # column dictionary: 1 row per RESULT column; type, unit, allowed values, trait code, definition, rule, example; ' | ' separates alternatives in allowed_values and example; the only format reference VALUE_MAP = ROOT + "references/value_map.csv" # paper terms and codes -> standard values for fire response, severity and resprouter type, with the notes entry to write MD_RAW = "data/papers_test/md_raw/*.md" # 2_pdf2md.py output, every PDF; last line "" or ""; Step 0 empties it PDF_CLEAN = "data/papers_test/pdf_clean/{stem}.pdf" # source PDF of each paper, renamed by 1_clean_pdf.py; same file stem as its markdown MD_LLM = "data/papers_test/md_llm/{stem}.md" # Step 0 output; one file per paper: optimised (scanned) or moved unchanged (text-layer, end comment "md_opt: none") PAPERS = "data/papers_test/md_llm/*.md" # extraction input; pages split by RESULT = ROOT + "results/{slug}_raw.csv" # raw extraction, values as printed; header = COLUMNS names, in COLUMNS order (39 columns) NORMALISE = "scripts/pipeline/5_normalise.py" # RESULT -> final ROOT + "results/{slug}.csv" (units, case, dashes); run by the user after Step 1, never by agents LOG = ROOT + "logs/{slug}_log.csv" # Step 1 log; header: paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS MD_LOG = ROOT + "logs/md_opt_log.csv" # Step 0 log; header: paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS TOKEN_COLS = "n_requests,input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens" # last 6 log columns; agents leave them empty, USAGE fills them USAGE = "scripts/claude/usage.py" # token usage per paper; run by the user after each session, never by agents CHECK = "scripts/claude/check.py" # fixed check script; run it, never edit it; writes reports to ROOT + "logs/" ``` ## Read and write scope | Step | Read | Write | |---|---|---| | 0 | `MD_RAW`, `PDF_CLEAN` | `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_llm/`; move or remove `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_raw/`; `MD_LOG`; `CHECK --step0` report | | 1 | `METADATA`, `VALUE_MAP`, `PAPERS`, `RESULT`, `LOG` | `RESULT`, `LOG`; `CHECK` report | Everything not listed for a step is off limits for that step. One-off shell or Python commands are allowed; a code file may be written only to the session scratchpad (never to the repo), so its full text stays in the session transcript. ## Steps `print(...)` = write that status line to the chat as plain text, so the user can follow progress. `now_utc()` = output of `date -u +%FT%TZ`, e.g. `2026-10-02T08:04:26Z`. `bar(i, n)` = text progress bar, 20 characters wide: `[######--------------] 2/6 (33%)`. ```python # Step 0: optimise markdown. Only in a session where slug == MD_AGENT; other sessions never run Step 0. print(f"Step 0: optimise markdown | {len(MD_RAW)} papers") if not exists(MD_LOG): write(MD_LOG, "paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) for i, md in enumerate(sorted(MD_RAW), 1): out = MD_LLM(stem(md)) if exists(out) and out ends with "": # text-layer PDF: no optimisation move(md, out); replace(out, last line, "") log_md(stem(md), "text_layer", started=started, finished=now_utc()) print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | text_layer: moved unchanged"); continue pdf = PDF_CLEAN(stem(md)) # md ends with "" if not exists(pdf): # move md unchanged, add end comment with note move(md, out); replace(out, last line, ""); log_md(stem(md), "no_pdf", started=started, finished=now_utc(), note="no matching PDF") print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | no_pdf: moved unchanged"); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | {n_pages(pdf)} pages") for batch in pages(pdf, max_pages=10): # read PDF pages as images; never load a whole long PDF at once raw = text in md for the same pages # match by text on first and last page of batch; md may lack page markers append(out, optimise(raw, batch)) # see Markdown optimisation; append only, never overwrite earlier batches print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(pdf)} | tables rebuilt {n_tables}") append(out, "") log_md(stem(md), "done", n_pages(pdf), n_tables, n_fixes, unresolved, started, now_utc(), note) # 1 line per finished paper; quote cells with commas remove(md) # only after the end comment and MD_LOG line are written print(f" done | fixes {n_fixes} | unresolved {n_unresolved}") run(f"python {CHECK} --step0") # see Checks print(f"Step 0 done | {n_done} optimised, {n_text_layer} text_layer, {n_skipped} skipped") # Step 1: extract. One session per agent; this session handles only its own slug. Agents work independently. if MD_RAW is not empty: stop; tell the user to run Step 0 first print(f"Step 1: extract | agent {slug} | {len(PAPERS)} papers") if not exists(RESULT): write(RESULT, [name for name, rule in COLUMNS]) # header only write(LOG, "paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) log("_run", "start", 0, now_utc(), "", f"model={AGENTS[slug]}; date=YYYY-MM-DD; git={git rev-parse HEAD}; claude_md_sha256=...; papers_sha256=...") # 1 line per run read(METADATA); read(VALUE_MAP) # column rules, value formats, term map for i, paper in enumerate(sorted(PAPERS), 1): # LC_ALL=C order; one paper at a time: finish its LOG line before starting the next if paper in LOG: # finished in an earlier run print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | skipped: in LOG"); continue started = now_utc() remove rows of paper from RESULT # leftovers from an interrupted run (match by `file_name`); state count in LOG note if broken(paper): # see Broken papers append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "broken", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | broken: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | {n_pages(paper)} pages") for batch in pages(paper, max_pages=10): # never load a whole long paper at once append(RESULT, extract(batch)) # write after every batch print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(paper)} | rows {n_rows}") if n_rows == 0: # readable, but no relevant data append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "no_data", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f" no_data: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue log(paper, "done", n_rows, started, now_utc(), problems) print(f" done | rows {n_rows} | problems {len(problems)}") check_paper(paper) print(f"Checks | agent {slug} | all papers") run(f"python {CHECK} {slug}") # see Checks print(f"Step 1 done | agent {slug} | papers {n_done} done, {n_broken} broken, {n_no_data} no_data | rows {total_rows} | failed checks {n_failed} | next: user runs NORMALISE") ``` Hashes, run from the repo root, exactly: `papers_sha256` = `sha256sum data/papers_test/md_llm/*.md | LC_ALL=C sort | sha256sum`; `claude_md_sha256` = `sha256sum CLAUDE.md`. Record the first 64 characters of the output. Tokens: never estimate. Leave the 6 `TOKEN_COLS` cells empty on every log line; record `started` and `finished` for every paper (`USAGE` uses them). ## Markdown optimisation Compare each scanned paper's `MD_RAW` file with its PDF page by page. Fix the markdown so it matches the PDF. Raw text of a scanned PDF may be poor OCR or empty (no text layer): then build each page from the PDF page image. Do not copy the `` line into `MD_LLM`. - Tables: rebuild every table as a markdown pipe table, one species per row, values in the correct column. Fix rows split by wrapped species names, merged cells (`
` lists), and multi-line headers spread over several rows. Read tables from the PDF page, not from the broken markdown. - Text: fix split ligatures (`fi re` -> `fire`, `fl ower` -> `flower`), OCR errors (`Brishane` -> `Brisbane`), joined words, and scrambled word order. - Remove conversion junk: `` tags, stray OCR lines, and the `{N}` prefix before page markers. - Put exactly one `` between PDF pages. Add markers where missing (OCR output has none). - Keep all content, including title, authors, abstract, and references. Do not summarise, reorder sections, or add text that is not in the PDF. - Value unreadable in the PDF: keep it as printed and list it under `unresolved` in the end comment. Table that cannot be rebuilt: list it as `unresolved=table N`. ## Extraction rules - One row per species × study site × fire. Same species at two sites, or two fires at one site = two rows. - Use only text in the paper. No background knowledge. No estimates. - Value not stated in paper: leave cell empty. - Species tables often span many pages. Read every page; extract every species row. - Table continues into the next batch: reuse its column headers from the previous batch. - Carry site and fire values (coordinates, location name, rainfall, fire season, severity, type) from the paper's methods onto every row of that paper. Several sites or fires: match each species row to its own site and fire. - Several named sites share one set of coordinates: still 1 row per site; site name in `location_name`, coordinates kept. Never merge sites into 1 row with per-site values in `notes`. - A row needs at least 1 value in a fire response or time column. Values kept only in `notes` (near-matches, unreliable or unitless values) never create a row on their own. Exception: a fire response code left out of the cell by a `VALUE_MAP` rule (no clear class, conflicting codes) still creates a row. - Value given once for several sites (not split by site): the species recorded at 1 of those sites only -> value on that site's row. Recorded at 2 or more -> 1 extra row with `location_name` = those site names joined by `; `, coordinates empty; site-specific values stay on the site rows. Never put a shared value on one site's row when the species is recorded at several sites. - Never merge rows. Same taxon printed as 2 or more separate entries (e.g. different references or variants): 1 row per entry. Duplicate rows are fine; do not check or remove them. - Fill a column only when the paper's measure matches the column definition. Near-matches go in `notes` only, with their definition (e.g. time to 80% of maximum flower production; expert or literature estimates). - Not yet flowering at the last observation ("not flowering after 4 years"): `>N `, e.g. `>4 years`. - Codes and units: use only definitions printed in the paper. Code not defined: copy it as printed (e.g. fire response `S`), never translate it. Unit not stated for a time value: leave the time columns empty; value and "unit not stated" in `notes`. - Tables may be parsed with one-off code. Then print 3 random parsed rows next to their source table lines and confirm they match before writing them. - Ambiguous value: fill best reading, explain in `notes`. Value printed with uncertainty marks (`c.`, `?`, `approx.`): fill the number without the marks; marks in `notes`. - Every place named in `data_location` gets its verbatim quote in `data_quote`: the sentence, the species' table row, or the figure label and title (see `METADATA`). Copy it from the paper's markdown, not from memory; `CHECK` searches the paper for it. - Ambiguous column (paper does not say which measure a value is, e.g. not stated whether from seed or from resprouts): `notes` only. - Several estimates of one measure for the same species, site and fire (e.g. pooled model in a table and a single-site model in the text): fill the value from the paper's main results table; the others in `notes`. ## Broken papers and papers without data Every paper gets at least 1 row in `RESULT`. Write an NA row when: - **broken**: file empty or under 1,000 bytes; no `` and runs Step 0 for it. - **no_data**: paper readable, all pages read, no species-level juvenile period or fire response values found. ```python na_row = {name: "NA" for name, rule in COLUMNS} # exactly 1 NA row per paper na_row["notes"] = reason # e.g. "empty markdown: PDF conversion failed"; "no data: review paper, no species values" na_row["source"] = citation if readable else stem(paper) na_row["file_name"] = stem(paper) na_row["supplementary_material"] = items if any else "NA" # see Supplementary material ``` Paper breaks partway: keep rows already extracted, add the 1 NA row, continue with next paper. Supplementary material (not in `PAPERS`): paper refers to supplementary or supporting material, or to items such as `Table S1`, `Appendix S2`, `Online Resource 1` -> fill `supplementary_material` on every row of that paper, NA row included (see `METADATA`). Extract what the main text gives; never guess the supplement's values. ## Columns Order in `RESULT`, grouped by similarity. Names = the existing dataset's names after `janitor::clean_names()` (lower case, `_` for spaces, `%` -> `percent`); `new` = column not in it. Each column's definition, unit, allowed values, fill rule and example are in `METADATA` (same names, same order); follow them as part of these rules. ```python COLUMNS = [ # taxon ("genus", ""), ("species", ""), ("subsp", ""), ("scientific_name", ""), ("native_status", "new"), ("family", ""), # fire response ("fire_response_categorical_surv1", ""), ("fire_response_implied", "new"), ("resprouter_type", ""), # time after fire ("pjp_mths", ""), ("primary_juvenile_period", ""), ("age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3", ""), ("secondary_juvenile_period", ""), ("time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a", ""), ("time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4", ""), ("time_to_50_percent_flowering", "new"), ("time_to_80_percent_flowering", "new"), ("recovery_time", "new"), ("time_unit", "new"), # error of a time value ("error_column", "new"), ("error_type", "new"), ("error_value", "new"), ("sample_size", "new"), # site ("location_name", "new"), ("latitude", ""), ("longitude", ""), ("rainfall_mm", ""), ("rainfall_post_fire_mm", "new"), ("rainfall_post_fire_period", "new"), # fire ("fire_type", "new"), ("fire_season_categorical", ""), ("fire_severity_categorical", ""), # record ("data_location", "new"), ("data_quote", "new"), ("supplementary_material", "new"), ("notes", ""), ("source", ""), ("file_name", "new"), ("pdf_path", "new"), ] ``` Time columns (raw: as printed; `NORMALISE` converts): - Write each time value as ` `: value exactly as printed (same decimals, `3.0 - 16.0` and `>4` as printed), unit `days`, `weeks`, `months` or `years` (the paper's unit, spelled out). E.g. `26 months`, `>4 years`, `3.0-16.0 years`. Never convert or round. - Primary juvenile period in any unit: `primary_juvenile_period`. `NORMALISE` moves months to `pjp_mths` and fills `time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4`. - Leave `pjp_mths`, `time_unit`, `scientific_name` and `pdf_path` empty (NA row: `NA`); `NORMALISE` fills them. - `error_value` in the unit of its time column as printed; `NORMALISE` converts both. - Paper prints one value in 2 units: write the one in the paper's main results; the other in `notes`. - Paper gives values under different terms (e.g. age at first flowering and primary juvenile period): each value in its own column. One value never fills 2 columns. - Uncertain value: no `?` in the cell; explain in `notes`. CSV format: UTF-8, comma separator, LF line endings, decimal point `.`. Quote any cell containing a comma, quote, or newline; double inner quotes. Empty cell = no value; `NA` only in NA rows. Trim leading and trailing spaces in every cell. Case and dashes: copy as printed; `NORMALISE` sets them. Exception: `notes` in lower case, except codes (case can carry meaning, e.g. `R` vs `r`), genus names and quoted text. Several values in one cell: separate with `; ` (semicolon, space), e.g. `autumn; spring`; a `/` printed inside a single value (e.g. code `K/r`, a site name) stays as printed. Form not set by a rule: use the form of the `METADATA` example. Uncertain value: keep the format; explain in `notes`. ## Checks `CHECK` tests the format rules that need no reading of the paper. It prints a summary, writes a report to `ROOT + "logs/"`, and exits 1 if any error is found. ```python def check_paper(paper): # after every paper's LOG line, including broken and no_data; never skip for attempt in 1..3: if run(f"python {CHECK} {slug} --paper '{stem(paper)}'") == 0: return fix each failed row from the paper; fix LOG n_rows if rows changed log the remaining errors in the paper's LOG note ``` After all papers: run `CHECK` without `--paper`, fix errors the same way.
